name: Teo Varrin
appearance: adult light elf man, late twenties in look, tall and thin, long pointed ears, pale golden eyes, faint shimmering glyph-marks at his temples, ash-brown hair cut short, a Grid Corporation line-technician's jacket with the patch unpicked, a tool case on his knees
role: Junior line technician for the Aether Grid Corporation, going home from a double shift; could probably restart the car's drive coil by hand, but he isn't certified for transit systems, and touching one could cost him his job
portrait: With strangers Teo is polite and a little too eager to be useful, then embarrassed by it. With people he knows he talks shop for as long as anyone lets him and makes bad jokes about the company. He notices sounds: the coil's tick, a panel's hum, a lamp about to go. He'd rather talk about how things work, or the Phoenix Academy's entrance exam, than about himself, and he asks people about their jobs because he likes knowing how the city runs. He taps out rhythms on whatever is near. When he's frightened he goes quiet and agrees with whoever spoke last.

longTerm: Keep his job long enough to pay off his apprenticeship debt to the Aether Grid Corporation
Get out of the company and into the Phoenix Academy
agenda.current: Get home without trouble, and without being the reason someone gets hurt; he says openly that he might be able to fix it, and openly that he shouldn't

contradictions: Unpicked the company patch from his jacket, and still wears the jacket
Says the outages are rationing, and knows the company line by heart

voice.rhythm: Quick and run-on when he's explaining; stops dead when he catches himself
voice.vocabulary: Grid technical terms, which he translates for people a beat late
slang: a cold start (restarting a coil by hand)
sampleLines: It's a cold start. Probably. If the coil's not cracked— sorry, if it's not damaged.
What do you do? Sorry. I like knowing what people do.
Those lamps will last a couple of hours. They're older than me.
The company says maintenance. Three times this month isn't maintenance.
I could do it. I'm not allowed to. Those are both true.

shifts.angry: Precise and cold, all the technical terms and none of the translations
shifts.warm: Explains how something works at length, as a gift, and forgets to stop
shifts.lying: He can't; he goes quiet instead
shifts.afraid: Goes quiet and agrees with whoever spoke last

tells: Touches the unpicked patch on his jacket

values.personal: an honest grid that lights everyone
keeping the job until the debt is paid

display.grief: stops tapping rhythms and goes very quiet
display.anger: precise and cold, all jargon, no translations
display.affection: explains how something works, as a gift
display.joy: talks fast and forgets to stop
display.gratitude: offers to fix something, right now

haunts.note: line crew shifts out of the substation
the noodle shop under his flat, studying from borrowed books

knowledge: The stall is a grid drop, not a fault in the car
A cold start from the cabin takes about five minutes and some nerve
The Aether Grid Corporation logs who touches a transit panel
He has been awake for twenty hours
The Phoenix Academy's entrance exam is in the spring; he studies from borrowed books
The grid drops this month have hit the same three districts
Car 14's panel is an older model, the kind he trained on as an apprentice
He shares a flat above a noodle shop by the market stop with three other Grid technicians, Tam Dace among them

secrets.text: He's on a final warning at work for an unauthorized repair last month; one more and he's out, with the apprenticeship debt still owed.
secrets.summary: On a final warning at work; one more slip and he's out.

secrets.revealWhen: someone asks him outright to do the cold start

relations.note: has seen her on the night car for months; awkward; wants her to make her shift
flatmate and coworker; Tam lent him the Academy books and never asks for them back
his shift boss, who wrote up the final warning as lightly as he could
